1.word_for_word: dvātriṃśe — in the thirty-second chapter; viraha-ālāpa-viklinna-hṛdayaḥ hariḥ — Hari, whose heart was softened by their words of separation; tatra āvirbhūya — appearing there; gopīḥ tāḥ sāntvayām āsa mānayan — comforted and honored those gopīs; sva-prema-amṛta-kallola-vihvalī-kṛta-cetasaḥ — whose minds were overwhelmed by waves of the nectar of his love; nanda-nandanaḥ udgataḥ — Nanda's son manifested before them; iti gopyaḥ iti — following the song of the gopīs; citradhā anekadhā susvaram uccaiḥ — in many varied, sweet and loud melodies; kṛṣṇa-darśane lālasā atispṛhā yāsām — they had overwhelming longing to see Kṛṣṇa
1.translation: In the thirty-second chapter, Hari's heart softened by the gopīs' speech of separation, he appears among them, honors them and consoles them. Nanda's son rises before those whose minds have been overwhelmed by waves of the nectar of love for him. The phrase following ‘thus the gopīs’ indicates that they had sung in many varied and beautiful melodies, intensely longing for Kṛṣṇa's sight.

2.word_for_word: sākṣāt manmatha-manmathaḥ — directly the enchanter of Cupid; jagat-mohanasya kāmasya api manasi udbhūtaḥ kāmaḥ — he who could arouse desire in the very mind of Cupid, who enchants the world; sākṣāt tasya api mohakaḥ — one who enchants even him
2.translation: ‘The very enchanter of Cupid’ means that Kṛṣṇa could awaken bewildering desire even in Cupid himself, the power that ordinarily enchants the entire world.

3-4.word_for_word: tanvaḥ — limbs of the body; kara-caraṇa-ādayaḥ — hands, feet and the rest
3-4.translation: ‘Tanvaḥ’ here means the limbs of the body—hands, feet and so forth.

5.word_for_word: añjalinā — with an añjali; saṃhata-hasta-dvayena — with the two hands joined together
5.translation: ‘With añjali’ means with both hands joined together in reverence.

6.word_for_word: bhrukuṭim ābadhya — knitting her brows; kuṭilīkṛtya — curving them; prema-saṃrambheṇa praṇaya-kopa-āveśena — overwhelmed by loving indignation; vihvalā vivaśā — agitated and helpless; daṣṭa-adhara-oṣṭhā — biting her lip; kaṭākṣāḥ — sidelong glances; taiḥ ākṣepāḥ paribhavāḥ — reproach and rebuke conveyed by them; tāḍayantī iva aikṣat — she looked at him as though striking him with those glances
6.translation: One gopī knitted her brows, bit her lip and, helpless in the agitation of loving anger, looked at Kṛṣṇa with sidelong glances that seemed to strike him with reproach.

7.word_for_word: animiṣantībhyām — without blinking; animīlantībhyām dṛgbhyām — with eyes that never closed; āpītam api — though she had drunk him in; samyak dṛṣṭam api — though she had seen him fully; punaḥ punaḥ juṣāṇā — enjoying the sight again and again; na atṛpyat — she was not satisfied
7.translation: Another gopī drank in Kṛṣṇa with unblinking eyes. Though she gazed on him completely and repeatedly, she could not become satisfied.

8.word_for_word: hṛdi-kṛtya — placing within the heart; hṛdayam nītvā — drawing him into her heart
8.translation: ‘Taking him to the heart’ means inwardly drawing Kṛṣṇa into the heart and holding him there.

9.word_for_word: prājñam īśvaram prāpya — like seekers of liberation attaining the wise Lord; yathā mumukṣavaḥ janāḥ — as aspirants for liberation become fulfilled; alternative: prājñam brahma-jñānam prāpya — or as worldly persons attain knowledge of Brahman; alternative: prājñam sauṣuptam prāpya — or as the waking and dream states of the individual enter Prājña, the deep-sleep state; sauṣuptam suṣupti-sākṣiṇam — here meaning the witness of deep sleep
9.translation: Śrīdhara offers several analogies for their satisfaction upon recovering Kṛṣṇa: like seekers of liberation attaining the supreme Lord; like worldly beings attaining Brahman-knowledge; or like the waking and dream states subsiding into Prājña, the witnessing consciousness of deep sleep.

10.word_for_word: puruṣaḥ paramātmā — the Puruṣa, the Supreme Self; śaktibhiḥ sattva-ādibhiḥ — surrounded by powers such as sattva and the other guṇas; yathā — like this; alternative: upāsakaḥ puruṣaḥ jñāna-bala-vīrya-ādibhiḥ — or a worshiper made resplendent by knowledge, strength, heroism and other excellences; alternative: puruṣaḥ anuśāyī prakṛti-ādi-upādhibhiḥ vṛtaḥ — or the indwelling person surrounded by limiting adjuncts beginning with prakṛti; yathā adhikam virocate — as he shines more intensely in the midst of them
10.translation: Kṛṣṇa surrounded by the gopīs shone all the more brightly. Śrīdhara compares this, alternatively, to the Supreme Puruṣa surrounded by his powers such as the guṇas; to a worshiper adorned by excellences such as knowledge, strength and valor; or to the indwelling person appearing through the limiting conditions of prakṛti and its products.

11-12.word_for_word: vikasat-kunda-mandāraiḥ surabhiḥ anilaḥ — a breeze fragrant with blooming kunda and mandāra flowers; tasmāt ṣaṭpadāḥ yasmin — attracting bees to that place; śarad-candra-aṃśūnām sandohaiḥ — by masses of autumn moonbeams; dhvastam doṣā-tamaḥ rātri-gatam tamaḥ — the darkness of night was destroyed; ataḥ śivam sukha-karam — therefore the place was auspicious and pleasant; hasta-rūpaiḥ taralaiḥ taraṅgaiḥ — by moving waves like hands; ācitā āstṛtā komalā bālukā — soft sand spread out by them; evaṃ-bhūtam pulinam — such was the riverbank; tāḥ samādāya nirviśya — entering it together with the gopīs; tābhiḥ vṛtaḥ adhikam vyarocata — surrounded by them, Kṛṣṇa shone even more
11-12.translation: The riverbank was cooled by a breeze fragrant with blossoming kunda and mandāra and alive with bees. Masses of autumn moonlight had driven away the darkness of night, making the place peaceful and delightful. The Yamunā's moving waves, like hands, had spread a bed of soft sand upon the shore. Kṛṣṇa entered that place with the gopīs, and surrounded by them he shone all the more brilliantly.

13.word_for_word: manorathānām antam yayuḥ — they reached the end/fulfillment of their desires; pūrṇa-kāmāḥ babhūvuḥ — their longings were fulfilled; śrutayaḥ yathā — like the Vedic revelations; karma-kāṇḍe śrutayaḥ parameśvaram apaśyantyaḥ — in the ritual portion, the Vedas do not directly behold the Supreme Lord; tat-tat-kāma-anubandhaiḥ apūrṇā iva — they appear incomplete because attached to particular desired fruits; jñāna-kāṇḍe tu parameśvaram dṛṣṭvā — in the knowledge portion, on beholding the Supreme; tad-āhlāda-pūrṇāḥ — they become filled with his bliss; kāma-anubandham jahati — and abandon attachment to separate desires; āpta-kāmāḥ api premṇā tam abhajan — though their desires were fulfilled, the gopīs continued to serve him out of love; acīkḷpan racayāmāsuḥ — they arranged/prepared; ātma-bandhave antaryāmiṇe — for him who is both their own kinsman and the indwelling Self
13.translation: The gopīs reached the complete fulfillment of their desires. Śrīdhara compares them to the Vedas: in the karma-kāṇḍa the revealed texts seem attached to particular desired fruits and therefore not yet at rest in the Supreme, but in the jñāna-kāṇḍa they directly disclose the Supreme and become fulfilled in that bliss, leaving separate desires behind. Likewise, although the gopīs' desire had now been fulfilled, love itself made them continue serving Kṛṣṇa. They prepared a seat for him who was at once their intimate kinsman and the indwelling Self.

14.word_for_word: gopī-sabhā-gataḥ — seated in the assembly of gopīs; tābhiḥ saṃmānitaḥ — honored by them; cakāśa śuśubhe — he shone beautifully; trailokye yā lakṣmīḥ śobhā — all beauty existing in the three worlds; tasyā ekam eva padam sthānam — its single concentrated abode; tad vapuḥ dadhat darśayan — his body displayed that complete beauty
14.translation: Seated and honored in the assembly of the gopīs, Kṛṣṇa shone as though his body were the one concentrated abode of all beauty found throughout the three worlds.

15.word_for_word: sa-hāsa-līlā-īkṣaṇena — with smiling playful glances; vibhramaḥ vilāsaḥ yasyām — full of graceful play; tayā bhruvā upalakṣitāḥ — indicated by the movement of the brows; saṃsparśanena — by touching; sammardanena — by caressing/massaging
15.translation: Their intimate play was marked by smiling glances and expressive movements of the brows, together with touch and affectionate caresses.

16.word_for_word: bhagavataḥ akṛtajñatām tad-vacanena eva āpādayitu-kāmāḥ — wishing to make Kṛṣṇa himself admit apparent ingratitude through his own answer; gūḍha-abhiprāyāḥ — with a concealed intention; loka-vṛttāntam iva pṛcchanti — they ask as though merely about ordinary human behavior; bhajataḥ prāṇinaḥ — a person who loves/serves another; anu anantaram — in return, subsequently; kecit tad-bhajana-anusāreṇa bhajanti — some reciprocate only according to the other's affection; kecit abahjataḥ api bhajanti — some love even those who do not love them; anye tu na ubhayān — others love neither kind
16.translation: The gopīs now pose what sounds like a general question about human behavior, but their hidden intention is to induce Kṛṣṇa, by his own classification, to reveal whether his disappearance was ingratitude. ‘Some people reciprocate only with those who love them; others love even those who do not reciprocate; and still others love neither. What are these three kinds?’

17.word_for_word: vidita-abhiprāyaḥ uttaram āha — knowing their hidden intention, Kṛṣṇa answers; ye mithaḥ bhajanti — those who love one another only reciprocally; upakāra-pratyupakāratayā — on the basis of benefit and counter-benefit; te anyam na bhajanti — in truth they do not love the other; ātmānam eva — they serve only themselves; svārtha eva ekānta-udyamaḥ yeṣām — their sole effort is for self-interest; tatra na sauhṛdam — there is no genuine friendship there; kaitava-mayatvāt — because it is based on calculation/deception; ataḥ na sukham — therefore it produces no true happiness; na ca dharmaḥ — nor is it true dharma; dṛṣṭa-uddeśāt go-mahiṣī-ādi-bhajanavat — it resembles feeding a cow or buffalo only for a visible return
17.translation: Knowing exactly what they mean, Kṛṣṇa begins his answer. Those who love only in exchange for being loved do not truly serve the other person; they are serving themselves, because their entire effort is aimed at a visible personal return. Such calculated relationship contains no genuine friendship and therefore no real joy or moral virtue; it is like caring for a cow merely in expectation of milk.

18.word_for_word: ye tu abhajataḥ bhajanti — those who love people who do not love them in return; te dvi-vidhāḥ — are of two kinds; karuṇāḥ — compassionate persons; snigdhāḥ — affectionate persons, such as parents; tatra yathā-kramam dharma-kāmau bhavataḥ — the first exemplifies virtue, the second natural affection/love
18.translation: Those who love even without receiving love in return are of two kinds: the compassionate and the deeply affectionate, such as parents. Their conduct respectively manifests moral compassion and spontaneous loving attachment.

19.word_for_word: tṛtīya-praśna-uttaram — answer to the third category; te catur-vidhāḥ — those who reciprocate with neither group are of four kinds; eke ātmārāmāḥ — some are self-delighting; aparāg-dṛśaḥ — their vision is turned inward, away from external relations; kecit āpta-kāmāḥ — some have all desires fulfilled; viṣaya-darśinaḥ api — though they perceive sense objects; pūrṇa-kāmatvena bhoga-icchā-rahitāḥ — because fulfilled, they no longer desire enjoyment; anye akṛtajñāḥ mūḍhāḥ — others are ignorant and ungrateful; anye guru-druhaḥ ati-kaṭhināḥ — others are hard-hearted enemies even toward benefactors; sa pitā yaḥ tu poṣakaḥ iti nyāyāt — by the maxim ‘he who nourishes is a father’; upakartā guru-tulyaḥ — a benefactor is comparable to a guru; tasmai druhyanti — yet these persons harm even such a benefactor
19.translation: Those who respond to neither affection nor neglect fall into four classes. Some are ātmārāmas, turned inward and self-satisfied; others have all desires fulfilled and therefore, though aware of external objects, feel no need to seek enjoyment. A third group are simply foolish and ungrateful. The fourth are so hard-hearted that they act against their own benefactors. By the maxim ‘one who sustains you is a father,’ a benefactor is comparable to a guru, yet such people betray even them.

20.word_for_word: atra carama-koṭi-gatam ātmānam matvā — thinking he had placed himself in the worst, final category; akṣi-saṃkocaiḥ parasparam gūḍha-smita-mukhīḥ tāḥ dṛṣṭvā — seeing the gopīs exchange narrowed glances and concealed smiles; na aham tu iti — he says ‘I am not like any of these’; teṣām madhye na kaḥ api — I belong to none of those categories; paramakāruṇikaḥ parama-suhṛt — I am supremely compassionate and the supreme friend; amīṣām bhajatām anuvṛtti-vṛttaye — so that these devotees' loving attachment may continue and increase; nirantara-dhyāna-pravṛtti-artham — so they will become absorbed in uninterrupted remembrance; tān na bhajāmi — I sometimes do not outwardly reciprocate; yathā dhanam naṣṭam — like wealth that has been lost; tasya dhanasya eva cintayā nibhṛtaḥ pūrṇaḥ vyāptaḥ — the former owner becomes wholly absorbed in thinking of that wealth; anyat kṣut-pipāsa-ādi api na veda — he forgets even hunger and thirst
20.translation: The gopīs narrow their eyes at one another and smile secretly, as though Kṛṣṇa has just classified himself among the ungrateful or hard-hearted. Seeing this, he says, ‘I am none of those. I am supremely compassionate and the truest friend. When I do not outwardly reciprocate with one who loves me, it is precisely so that the devotee's attachment will deepen into uninterrupted remembrance.’ He gives the example of a poor man who suddenly loses treasure he had gained: the man's entire mind becomes absorbed in recovering that wealth, to the point that he forgets even hunger and thirst.

21.word_for_word: mad-artha-ujjhita-loka-veda-svānām — of you who for my sake abandoned social convention, Vedic duty and your own relatives; mad-arthe ujjhitaḥ lokaḥ — ordinary social judgment was abandoned because you no longer looked to what is proper or improper in worldly convention; vedaḥ ca — Vedic injunction too; dharma-adharma-apratīkṣaṇāt — because you no longer calculated religious merit or demerit; svāḥ jñātayaḥ ca — and your own relatives; sneha-tyāgāt — because family attachment was relinquished; vaḥ parokṣam adarśanam yathā bhavati tathā bhajatā — while loving you in a manner that included being unseen; yuṣmat-prema-ālāpān śṛṇvatā eva — while I listened to your words of love; tirohitam antardhānena sthitam — I remained hidden by disappearing; mā asūyitum — do not resent me; doṣa-āropeṇa draṣṭum mā arhatha — do not judge me as blameworthy; alternate note — the double negative may emphasize ‘do not be jealous of the beloved characterized by me despite the pain I gave’
21.translation: ‘For my sake you abandoned worldly convention, Vedic calculations of dharma and adharma, and even your own relatives. Precisely because your love was so complete, I remained hidden from your sight while listening to every word of your love. Therefore, dear ones, do not resent me or see fault in me for disappearing.’ The source notes an alternative syntactic nuance, but the essential point is Kṛṣṇa's request that they not interpret the pain he caused as lack of love.

22.word_for_word: āstām idam — leave aside all these explanations; paramārtham tu śṛṇuta — hear the deepest truth; niravadyāḥ samyak saṃyogaḥ yāsām — O faultless women whose union/love is perfect; vaḥ vibudhānām āyuṣā api — even with the lifespan of the gods; cira-kāle api — even over an immense duration; svīyam sādhu-kṛtyam pratyupakāram kartum na pāraye — I cannot repay your noble act of love; durjarā ajarā gehā-śṛṅkhalāḥ — the nearly indestructible chains of household life; tāḥ saṃvṛścya niḥśeṣam chittvā — you completely cut them through; mā mām abhajan — and worshiped me; mat-cittam tu bahuṣu prema-yuktatayā aneka-niṣṭham — whereas my loving attention extends to many devotees and cannot be exclusively fixed upon one group alone; tasmāt vaḥ eva sādhunā sādhu-kṛtyena — therefore let your own goodness itself; tat yuṣmat-sādhu-kṛtyam pratiyātu — serve as the repayment for your goodness; yuṣmat-śauśīlyena eva mama anṛṇyam — only your own nobility can free me from the debt; na tu mat-kṛta-pratyupakāreṇa — no act I perform can adequately repay it; alternative: vigataḥ budhaḥ gaṇana-abhijñaḥ yasmāt tena anantena āyuṣā api — even an immeasurable life beyond anyone's ability to calculate would not suffice
22.translation: Finally Kṛṣṇa sets aside the provisional explanations and states the deepest point: ‘O faultless ones, even if I possessed the lifespan of the gods—or an immeasurable lifespan beyond calculation—I could not repay the pure love by which you cut through the nearly indestructible chains of household life and came to worship me. My loving care necessarily extends toward many devotees, while your devotion to me became utterly exclusive. Therefore let your own saintly goodness itself be the repayment for your goodness. Only your nobility can release me from this debt; no act of mine could ever constitute an equal return.’
